986.t: Standout in a small Washington State town
986.s: He was a local musical standout but far behind players elsewhere; he believes everyone has a time when the music chooses them.
986.ch: Coming up: Indiana and William Paterson
986.q: I’m not going to lie about that. I was certainly a musical standout, but compared to what. I mean in a small town in Washington State where nobody my age knew how to improvise at all, really to speak of. You know the fact that I knew how to play a blues scale and do something semi-convincingly, you…

911.t: Reluctantly choosing the saxophone and learning through lessons
911.s: Musical parents, fifth-grade band day, picking the saxophone because it looked expensive, and private lessons driving his practice.
911.q: Yeah well the ironic thing is when, you know I have fairly musical parents. They’ve both done choir. My dad was in the University of Michigan Men’s Glee Club chorus. My dad’s a pastor and so he was always involved with music at the church and things like that. And I remember growing up and doing a…

399.t: Late start as a musician: childhood guitar and parties with Compay Segundo
399.s: Conte never planned a music career; in Cuba he had guitar lessons, played percussion, and watched friends of his father like Compay Segundo at house parties, then felt lost in Hollywood.
399.ch: Finding the drums at Los Angeles City College
399.q: It was – well I have to explain to you because I never thought I was going to be a musician. I’m a really late guy. A super late guy. I played music since I was a little boy. I played guitar also, I had lots of guitar lessons when I was in Cuba. I was able to learn how to play son and some things…

540.t: Growing up in Chicago with musician parents; starting trumpet
540.s: Both parents were musicians; Gardner took piano, then at nine insisted on trumpet and got one from his father.
540.q: Yeah. As a matter of fact it’s funny, I just answered that question earlier today in Doc’s history class. And it was around the time when I was about maybe a junior in high school that I said I think music is the direction I’m going to go. Both my parents are musicians and educators as well. My…

964.t: Cutting tape as a kid and loving group studio work
964.s: His father bought a Webcor recorder, he learned to splice tape, and he preferred collaborative studio work to solitary cello practice.
964.q: I was a kid. I remember being in my mom's house when I was little and my dad bought me a Webcor portable tape recorder. It was the first one that could sit like this on a desk. I mean it wasn't gigantic, it was just like this. And it had reel—to—reel. And I remember I played the cello and then I…

545.t: Discovering jazz on Chicago's South Side; piano and flute lessons
545.s: Mandel grew up near the Stony Island divide, drawn to Ramsey Lewis, R&B, Miles, Coltrane and Dolphy, thinking of jazz as dramatic and abstract. He had piano and flute lessons.
545.q: Well I was listening to Ramsey Lewis and “The In Crowd” and rhythm & blues music, it was on the local radio. I grew up in Chicago and I lived in a community that was on the South Side of Chicago so it was a neighborhood that was divided by Stony Island Avenue which is a large commercial street, and…

498.t: Never playing for dancers; all he wanted was the piano
498.s: As a young hippie jazz kid he never played for dancers and only wanted to play piano, which still moves him.
498.q: We were a little stoned out, like little stoned hippie jazz kids. We didn’t play for dancers, we just sat around looking cool, playing little dives and thinking we were the cat’s ass. I mean you know I didn’t know even dance existed. I didn’t know anything existed. In fact I had — I ran into an old…

1047.t: Kindergarten aha moment and Mrs. Marge
1047.s: In kindergarten a teacher told her she would be a great singer but not to get the big head.
1047.q: More oh no, than aha. But I will say that I think aha moments come when you realize that someone believes in you. I think that was my aha moment. And you kind of just put together a bunch of different aha moments until you actually say okay, this is what I’m going to do. So I’d say my first aha…

506.t: Seeing Georges Miquelle play Dvorak with the Detroit Symphony
506.s: Hearing the French cellist at fourteen convinces Carter he can do that himself.
506.q: Yeah, great sound, the orchestra sounded fabulous and this huge building that I'd never been in this size before, with all these people around. Just the whole musical air was really crisp. They were … there was no fooling around. They were really intent on doing this particular solo piece. I think…

136.t: Lead sheets, Mr. Fukui's Teddy Wilson record and leaving for Fukuoka
136.s: She could not read chord symbols; collector Fukui played her Teddy Wilson, her first jazz, and she moved to Fukuoka at seventeen against her father's anger.
136.ch: First jobs and learning jazz in Beppu and Fukuoka
136.q: [Army Navy] Hit Kit [of Popular Songs] is one of the things that the servicemen … every month or maybe twice a month, I‟m not quite sure, it was American hit songs.
